title: Engineered enzyme strips advanced glycation end-products to reverse age-related protein damage
description: An engineered enzyme that removes advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) from proteins is reversing a long-standing driver of tissue stiffening and age-related dysfunction. AGE-clearing enzymes could address cross-linking damage that current interventions leave untouched.

title: GPR40 agonism regenerates the aged thymus, restoring T-cell production in mice
description: A small-molecule GPR40 (fatty-acid receptor) agonist reversed thymic involution in aged mice, regenerating thymic tissue and restoring T-cell output. Rejuvenating the thymus is a direct lever on immune aging and inflammaging.

title: Boosting aquaporin-4 improves the brain's glymphatic waste clearance and cuts tau pathology
description: Enhancing aquaporin-4 water channels improved glymphatic drainage of cerebrospinal fluid and reduced tau pathology in mice, while loss of glymphatic drainage tracked Alzheimer's progression in patients. Brain waste-clearance is emerging as a tractable neurodegeneration target.

title: Aging clocks face a reliability reckoning as short-term stress skews methylation results
description: New work shows short-term biological stresses can significantly distort methylation-based epigenetic age, and a major review maps the capabilities and limits of aging clocks. Measurement noise has direct implications for trials that use clocks as endpoints.

title: Longevity's safety reckoning: an IV-infusion death, an unvetted peptide craze, and Montana's right-to-try expansion
description: A death after a NAD+ 'longevity infusion,' a surge of unvetted injectable peptides, and Montana recruiting longevity leaders to expand right-to-try access underline a widening gap between consumer longevity marketing and clinical evidence.

title: Jose Pedro Castro on inflammation as a driver of aging
description: An interview with Dr. Jose Pedro Castro on how chronic inflammatory processes contribute to core aging mechanisms.

title: Short-term stresses may undermine epigenetic clock results
description: Biological fluctuations from short-term stress can significantly affect the reliability of methylation-based epigenetic aging measurements.

title: Montana's right-to-try law enters a new phase with longevity industry advisors
description: Montana's experimental-treatment review board recruited three longevity industry leaders to help expand access to experimental therapies.

title: How the immune system makes sun damage worse
description: Neutrophil extracellular traps worsen ultraviolet skin damage; inhibiting them was protective in studies.

title: NYC woman dies after receiving a NAD+ 'longevity infusion'
description: A death following an intravenous NAD+ infusion highlights the dangers of unproven longevity treatments given outside proper medical settings.

title: More autophagy reduces toxin-induced kidney failure in aged mice
description: Enhancing autophagy protected against acute kidney injury in older mice, countering an age-related decline in cellular cleanup.

title: The progress and future of biological aging clocks
description: A comprehensive review examines the development, capabilities, and limitations of biological aging measurement technologies.

title: Structured training erases parts of the muscle aging signature
description: Planned exercise regimens protected against specific aspects of muscle aging better than general physical activity alone.

title: Gabriel Cian on building the 2060 longevity investment ecosystem
description: A follow-up interview on how the longevity investment ecosystem is evolving and lessons from the prior year's Forum.

title: Stem-cell-derived exosomes fight liver disease in mice
description: Researchers used stem-cell-derived exosomes to combat harmful metabolic changes in liver tissue.

title: Activating GPR40 fights thymic involution in mice
description: Targeting the GPR40 receptor delayed thymic aging, potentially supporting immune-system maintenance in older organisms.

title: A conservative view on the current peptide craze
description: Commentary on the regulatory gaps allowing unvetted injectable peptides to be marketed with minimal evidence.

title: Poor sleep quality correlates with pace of aging, but causation is mixed
description: Sleep decline correlates with faster aging, though shared genetic factors may partly explain the relationship.

title: Age-related mitochondrial dysfunction reframed as a failure of adaptability
description: A model proposing mitochondrial aging stems from an inability to adjust ATP production to reduced cellular demand.

title: Thymulin restrains inflammation but declines with age
description: The thymus-derived peptide thymulin suppresses inflammatory signaling and supports immune response, but falls with age.

title: Loss of glymphatic CSF drainage correlates with Alzheimer's progression
description: Impaired brain-fluid drainage measured via MRI correlated with cognitive decline in Alzheimer's patients.

title: Reviewing what is known of immune system aging
description: An overview of immune-organ decline, reduced lymphocyte production, and inflammaging mechanisms.

title: Clonal hematopoiesis (CHIP) linked to accelerated epigenetic age
description: Blood-cell mutations correlated with accelerated epigenetic aging measures in older adults.

title: SORLA upregulation as a possible route to treat tauopathies
description: Increasing SORLA protein reduced tau accumulation and neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease models.

title: Gut microbiome composition correlates with epigenetic clock results
description: Specific bacterial species predicted biological aging pace independent of chronological age.

title: NewLimit raises $435M ahead of its first clinical trial
description: Epigenetic-reprogramming startup NewLimit raised $435M to advance toward its first human trial, one of the year's largest longevity rounds.

title: Retro Biosciences valued at $1.8B in latest raise
description: Cellular-reprogramming company Retro Biosciences reported a fundraising round valuing it at $1.8 billion.
